lines.en: : No, idiot. A huge, lit-up tree.
: Oh, neat. But did you really have to stay silent the whole way here just so you could clap back at me with that response?
: Anything for the bit, Imani. Our fans would love this.
: The fact that we have fans at all is kind of impressive given that nothing we’ve ever done has been televised or publicly available anywhere.
: That’d be crazy, though. Right? If we were just part of some TV show or movie this entire time and didn’t even know about it.
: Oh, like the Truman Show! That sounds fun. I hope they censored the foursome scene, though. I wouldn’t want Kirin masturbating to it.

: You know, I feel like that would actually explain a lot about being here. The barriers...the space war...the fact that there always needs to be something tragic happening. This really does feel like the setup to a film.
: Does that make me the love interest then?
: Why not the protagonist?
: Me? A biracial, bisexual woman? Are you kidding? Just think of what Twitter would say.
: Yeah, you’re right. I hesitate to call myself a safer bet concerning anything other than ratings, though. But maybe one day- when the writer in charge of us no longer feels beholden to the masses.
: So that’s it then? We’re just accepting the Truman Show as our new reality?
: Yeah. Start looking for a door built into the sky or something. I’m about ready for the credits to roll.
That huge, lit-up tree smiles down at us in all of its Christmassy glory, but we’re too focused on feeding off one another to realize it.

I know it’s only been a couple hours at this point, but I’m having fun. Imani’s great when it comes to adapting to whatever mood I’m in. And that makes it easier to find comfort in borderline nothingness.
But maybe that’s because she’s my co-star in this new rom-com of a life. They wouldn’t have cast someone who didn’t have good chemistry with me.
It all feels too real to be just that, though. Which is why I can joke about things like doors in the sky and ratings and whatnot as a staged reality would be far too convenient to ever be true.
Imagine it was, though.
Imagine we did find a door. And the moment I passed through it, everyone I’ve ever come to know just smiled and collected their paycheck — leaving me to fend for myself outside my lifelong bassinet.
I’d be helpless out there. It’d be hilarious. But still...I think I’d be open to giving it a shot.
A world where no one loves me sounds nice. I’m sure I’d be saying the opposite if the tables were turned, though.
It’s easy to want what you don’t have when there’s a permanent baseline of misery stretched across the metaphorical floor of your metaphorical existence.
And I think I’d spend a little less time tripping over it if I could be distracted by the need to find a companion rather than just waiting for one to come to me.
I wonder how someone like Imani would view me outside of Kumon-mi. Would all those red flags I mentioned earlier push her away? Or would they obscure me just enough to make me look approachable?
If they did...I think she’d have a better shot out there.
I think I’d be more inclined to latch onto this feeling and never let it go than I am in this world. Because on the outside, I’m not saying I wouldn’t have seven billion choices.
I’m saying I’d lack the patience to sift through them all with the looming threat of mortality weighing me down.
She’s the easiest way for me to start over.
I’ve just come so far here that doing so would feel like one sin I could never pray away.
: I think this is the part where you say that clichéd line about how “the moon is beautiful” or whatever.
: Nah. If this really is a movie, I’m sure that’s already been used by now.
: Maybe hit me with the good ole’ Casablanca then? Here’s looking at you, kid...or however it goes.
: I’m not even sure that would fit the context of this scene since there’s no pressing threat of me leaving you behind.
: Well, that’s comforting. Because finding another guy in Kumon-mi sounds way too hard and I don’t think I could settle for Rika given the age gap.
: There’s a bit of an age gap between us too, you know.
: Naaah. Ours is realistic. And by the time I hit menopause, you’ll probably already have a bad back and won’t be able to screw me as hard anyway.
: So what I’m hearing is that we belong together because we’re both going to start physically decaying around the same time?
: Yeah, pretty much. But I think there’s a lot more than just that that makes us work. Assuming you ever want to actually go out with me and not just hit it all the time.
: Sorry, Imani. Kumon-mi High prohibits me from dating a coworker. Probably.
: He says, despite having not been my co-worker since prior to last Christmas.
: I’m still your superior on paper, though. And that paper may very well be shredded the moment the principal finds out we come into contact with one another’s genitals on occasion.
: You have such a way with words, Senpai. Staring up at the moon while hearing you talk about genitals is really making my heart flutter.
: I’d say that just looking at you is making mine do that, but I feel like I wouldn’t be able to see you at all if it weren’t for the bright yellow outfit you’re wearing.
: I strategically chose this so you wouldn’t lose me. Seems it’s paying off in spades, huh?
: Seems so. Are you still having a good time now that I’ve pulled you all the way over here to talk about movies and age gaps, though?
: Or should we start winding this down because I get progressively more unlikable with every passing minute?
: That ain’t true, Senpai. My feelings for you are kind of peaking right now if we’re being honest. Which we probably shouldn’t since I know you want to keep me as a friend. But yeah. You’re great.
: If you really want me to date you, you’re going to have to stop complimenting me. The quickest way to my heart seems to be just bossing me around and reminding me of how much I suck all the time.
: You like Wakana that much, huh?
: That’s...not who I was thinking of. But yeah, I guess it does apply to her too. She’d also be a good match for me if she hadn’t spent her whole life banging a would-be Olympian.
: Now’s the best chance you have to steal her, you know.
: Imani, come on.
: What? I’m not endorsing it. I love Osako.
: I’m just saying, if you really think she’d be a good match for you...and you think screwing her for the rest of forever would bring you happiness...what are you waiting for?
: Are you telling me you’d betray your friends if it brought you closer to happiness?
: It’s not about betraying them, Senpai. It’s about doing what’s best for you.
: No one likes letting other people down. But it still happens every day because it kind of has to for anyone to ever get what they want.
: Otherwise, we’d have a bunch of people running around with unfulfilled wishes — dwelling on “what ifs” and “what could have beens” instead of focusing on where they are now. And with whom.
: I guess that explains why you’ve always been so open about your feelings for me then.
: Not always. It took me a while to summon the courage to confess to you — if you even want to call it that. I’m just better at reasoning than I am at acting.
: Then I guess we’ve found one thing we don’t have in common since I’m the exact opposite. Acting, I can do. But rationalizing even the simplest things feels like a mental obstacle course some days.
: Maybe you need a change of pace then?
: Is this the part where you proclaim that you can be that change of pace? Because it would be a good time for that.
: Yeah.
: Just not in the way you’re probably thinking.
: Hm?
: What would you say if I told you I had a solution to like a million of your problems in the palm of my hands, but I was intentionally not revealing it because I didn’t want to betray anyone?
: I’d say that’s a convenient turn of events and extremely topical given what we were discussing one minute ago. And also that it is likely not true.
: Are you happier now that you’re not teaching anymore, Senpai?
: Not...really? But there are also several other factors contributing to that. And it certainly doesn’t help always worrying about having to come back.
: Wakana gave you a deadline, right? The...beginning of the next school year or something?
: It’s not really the deadline I’m worried about. It’s that I’m constantly letting everyone down by postponing my return over and over again.
: It’s not just Wakana either. You add to it. The girls add to it. And then I add to it on those early mornings where I just wander around town remembering where I’m supposed to be.
: But I’m afraid of coming back because I don’t think it will fix that creeping dread of never going anywhere...Or the repetition of living through the same days over and over again.
: Which isn’t even mentioning how you’re a better teacher than I ever was.
: I don’t know. There’s a lot wrong with my life right now, and even more is changing. And I probably would’ve come back to school already if I thought that was the key to changing that.
: Why not just rip the Band-aid off then?
: Why not quit?
: You don’t actually-
: I think you should do what’s best for you. And I think that Wakana and I have both been way too selfish in pushing you to come back because that’s what we want.
: We miss you. You know that. But, and I know you’re going to disagree with this, neither one of us knows you as well as you do.
: We can tell ourselves we know what’s best for you, sure. So can all of the girls. But if you’re living with the constant pressure of having to return to school...and that’s killing you?
: Just stop.
: It’s okay to walk away, Senpai. Responsibility is one thing, yeah. But an even bigger thing is figuring out what the hell you want to do with your life.
: And, being someone who actually likes teaching, I’m not sure that this is right for you.
: You’re just saying that because you’re gunning for my job.
: No, Senpai. I’m not.
: Then...you’re just saying it because it cancels out that thing I said earlier about not dating coworkers.
: No, Senpai. I’m-
: Well, actually, that one’s true.
: But that’s still not the point!
: At the end of the day, all I really want is for you to not feel like every day is just a repeat of the one before it.
: Well, I’ve got very bad news for you.
: Like 40%% of your personality is having bad news. You’re constantly talking yourself out of everything that could potentially bring you joy.
: But school seems to be like the one thing you talk yourself into that doesn’t bring you joy. And it feels like you’re only there because you believe that’s where you’re meant to be.
: Wakana would kill me for saying this and...I kind of hate myself for it since it feels like I’m convincing you to spend less time with me...
: But maybe the time we spend together will be more fulfilling without that creeping dread latching onto your ankles the whole time?
: I don’t really get religious often, but there’s a quote from the Bible that’s like...
: “When times are good, be happy; but when times are bad, consider — God has made the one as well as the other. Therefore, a man cannot discover anything about his future.”
: “In this meaningless life of mine I have seen both of these: a righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.”
: “Do not be overrighteous, neither be overwise-- why destroy yourself? Do not be overwicked, and do not be a fool-- why die before your time?”
: That’s a really long quote to remember for someone who doesn’t get religious very often.
: Yeah, well...I’ve heard it a thousand times, so...
: Either way, I don’t want you to dwell on this shit for so long that you turn into some giant ball of uncertainty and negativity. I want you to live. And I want you to let yourself live.
: So if that means cutting certain cords...even if those cords are connected to all of us who care about you...maybe that’s what needs to be done? Do you see what I mean?
: I do. But, question — is this one of those things you’ve been thinking about for longer than you let on? Or did all of this really just come to you now?
: Beats me! Anyway, here’s a present.
: Where were you even keeping this? And why do I suddenly not feel the need to further press you about that thing I just asked?
: Probably because you’ve already come up with an answer. Don’t worry, though. I’m not going to make you reveal it tonight. Take as much time as you need.
: Can I open this now or are you going to make me wait until I get home?
: You can open it now. Fair warning, though — I am just as bad at gift-giving as I am asking people out on dates. Please see it as “endearing” rather than “careless.”
: I’m sure it’s fine. I understand that I’m a hard person to shop for.
: Also, in lieu of giving me a present, you can just fuck me or whatever. Rain check, though.
: Imani.

: I know, I know. Your balls must be blue as hell having to suffer through my apparent “peak cuteness.” But I cannot control the clock, Senpai. This is merely a side-effect of the cruel joke that is humanity.
: No, Imani. This is a pocketknife.
: Yeah. Cool, right?
: I mean...sure? But this is more of a Noriko gift than one for me.
: Noriko’s the one who helped me pick it out, actually.
: Why?
: Bro, you said it yourself. You ain’t easy to shop for. And the Internet says dudes in their thirties like pocketknives.
: It was either that or craft soap, and I wasn’t about to drop 5,000 yen on showers I ain’t allowed to join you for.
: What am I going to do with it?...
: Give it to Ami! She was having a damn good time cutting through some meat earlier. She’ll know what to do with it.
: You good, Senpai? Should I have gotten the soap instead?
: I’m good.
: Just...
: Felt like I was about to remember something...
We stayed there and stared at the tree for another thirty minutes or so, talking more about whether or not I should come back to school.
And honestly, I don’t know yet.
Imani brought up a lot of good points, but...
If that’s not what I want to spend my life doing, what should I do?
What else could I do?
If what I’ve learned is true, which I’m pretty sure it is, teaching is essentially all I’ve ever done.
Granted, I do currently have an eternity to take up something else, so...
I don’t know. I’ll think more about it later. And I’ll have plenty of time to do so, seeing as Imani is too biologically impaired to invite me back to her place to really end our date tonight.
She seemed fine with it, though.
: AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!
: TONIGHT TOTALLY WOULD HAVE BEEN THE NIGHT!!!!!! CURSE THIS BODY!!!! CURSE THIS WORLD!!!! HOW LONG MUST I REMAIN UNFUCKED FOR?!?!?!
: Uhh, Imani? Everything okay in there?
And I’m sure she’s already over it by now as there will be plenty more opportunities for me to annihilate her lower body in the future.
